778

780	|---|---|---|
781	| MySQL 8 | job table: the single source of truth for job state | parameters, input checksums, status, attempt number and token, lease, accepted attempt (and so its run id), error |

783	| Worker | runs the existing CLIs (`etf_risk.windows` → `etf_risk.spark_pipeline` → `etf_risk.verify`) in a subprocess for each job it claims | one job at a time on this machine, for memory |

787	
788	```mermaid
789	flowchart LR
790	    S[submit CLI] -->|insert job as queued| DB[(MySQL jobs)]
791	    S -->|publish job id, wait for confirmation| K[[Kafka topic]]
792	    S -->|then set published_at| DB
793	    K --> W[worker]
794	    W -->|claim: new attempt token and lease| DB
795	    W -->|commit offset after the claim| K
796	    W --> P["windows → spark_pipeline → verify"]
797	    P --> O[run folder per attempt]
798	    W -->|accept result if the token still matches| DB
799	    R[reconciler] -->|expired lease or unconfirmed publish| DB
800	    R -->|republish| K
801	    Q[summary query] -->|hit| C[(Redis)]
802	    Q -->|miss: Spark SQL on paired| O
803	```
804	
805	**Guarantee.** Each job accepts at most one result. A successfully completed job
806	has one accepted result. A job may execute more than once: Kafka delivers at
807	least once, and a lease can expire while a slow worker still runs.
808	
809	- **Attempt tokens.** Every claim writes a new attempt token and attempt number
810	  in one conditional update. Lease renewal and the final status write both
811	  require that token; an update that matches no row means the worker was fenced
812	  off: it stops, and its outputs are not accepted.
813	- **Run ids include the attempt**, so attempts never share an output folder, and
814	  the pipeline never overwrites outputs.
815	- **Manual offset commits.** Auto-commit is off; the worker commits the Kafka
816	  offset only after its claim succeeded, or after deciding the job needs nothing
817	  (already succeeded, or held by a live lease). A worker that dies before
818	  committing gets the job redelivered.
819	- **Publish confirmation.** The producer (`acks=all`, idempotence on) waits for
820	  Kafka's delivery confirmation before `published_at` is set; otherwise the
821	  reconciler publishes again. With one broker, `acks=all` means that broker
822	  wrote the message; there is no replica.
823	
824	**Engineering questions**
825	
826	- **E1.** Does each job accept at most one result, and does every successfully
827	  completed job have exactly one, even when jobs execute more than once?
828	- **E2.** After a worker crash (before or after its claim), a broker restart or a
829	  database restart, how long until the job runs again and finishes, and is any
830	  job lost or accepted twice?
831	- **E3.** How much latency does a result cache save for repeated summary queries
832	  compared with a warm Spark session, at which hit rates, and what happens when
833	  Redis is down?
834

838	  matches a reference run by content (Parquet files differ in bytes between runs).

790	    S[submit CLI] -->|insert job as queued| DB[(MySQL jobs)]
791	    S -->|publish job id, wait for confirmation| K[[Kafka topic]]
792	    S -->|then set published_at| DB
793	    K --> W[worker]
794	    W -->|claim: new attempt token and lease| DB
795	    W -->|commit offset after the claim| K
796	    W --> P["windows → spark_pipeline → verify"]
797	    P --> O[run folder per attempt]
798	    W -->|accept result if the token still matches| DB
799	    R[reconciler] -->|expired lease or unconfirmed publish| DB
800	    R -->|republish| K
801	    Q[summary query] -->|hit| C[(Redis)]
802	    Q -->|miss: Spark SQL on paired| O

805	**Guarantee.** Each job accepts at most one result. A successfully completed job
806	has one accepted result. A job may execute more than once: Kafka delivers at
807	least once, and a lease can expire while a slow worker still runs.

809	- **Attempt tokens.** Every claim writes a new attempt token and attempt number
810	  in one conditional update. Lease renewal and the final status write both
811	  require that token; an update that matches no row means the worker was fenced
812	  off: it stops, and its outputs are not accepted.
813	- **Run ids include the attempt**, so attempts never share an output folder, and
814	  the pipeline never overwrites outputs.
815	- **Manual offset commits.** Auto-commit is off; the worker commits the Kafka
816	  offset only after its claim succeeded, or after deciding the job needs nothing
817	  (already succeeded, or held by a live lease). A worker that dies before
818	  committing gets the job redelivered.
819	- **Publish confirmation.** The producer (`acks=all`, idempotence on) waits for
820	  Kafka's delivery confirmation before `published_at` is set; otherwise the
821	  reconciler publishes again. With one broker, `acks=all` means that broker

830	  job lost or accepted twice?
831	- **E3.** How much latency does a result cache save for repeated summary queries

865	    354–478 MiB for Kafka, over three runs; the run of commit e2806bd gave 398 and

868	    Kafka reached 516 MiB, 80%, in a session that also ran three mutation checks
869	    against it, which create many short-lived topics and consumer groups.
870	  - About two hours of repeated runs on the same containers reached 511 MiB for
871	    MySQL, 99% of its budget. Its anonymous memory had grown from 264 MiB after
872	    one run to 313 MiB; the rest was page cache. Kafka reached 404 MiB, 63%.
873	    Neither container hit its limit.
874	  - MySQL's 511 MiB shows limited headroom. It is not evidence that longer runs
875	    stay within 512 MiB: its anonymous memory was still growing, and nothing

**Implemented:**
- the pipeline and three Spark SQL analyses of its results;
- a Docker image;
- four performance experiments: the stride experiment ([experiments.md](experiments.md)), the
  shuffle-partition experiment ([partition-experiment.md](partition-experiment.md)), the pandas
  baseline ([pandas-baseline.md](pandas-baseline.md)) and the caching experiment
  ([caching-experiment.md](caching-experiment.md));
- the figures, results write-up and demo of Stage 4 ([results.md](results.md), [demo.md](demo.md)).

**In progress: an optional systems extension with MySQL, Kafka and Redis (§11).** Implemented so
far:
- the job queue: the job table, Kafka delivery and the reconciler ([job-table.md](job-table.md),
  [job-queue.md](job-queue.md)), and a worker that runs the real pipeline under a watchdog and a
  host execution lock ([worker-pipeline.md](worker-pipeline.md));
- the recovery study, documented ([recovery-part-a.md](recovery-part-a.md),
  [recovery-part-b.md](recovery-part-b.md)), with supporting correctness observations for E1;
- the Redis result cache ([result-cache.md](result-cache.md)), and its experiment E3, with one
  valid formal batch ([result-cache-part-b.md](result-cache-part-b.md)).

Outstanding (§11, open items): valid formal E2 recovery-time evidence, a representative
validation of the native processes' memory, and two unresolved intermittent failures of the
baseline collector's tests (§10).

# Demo

A short walk-through on the machine that holds the project's data: the tests, the figures and their
check, the SQL analyses of the run of record, and a small pipeline run with its independent check.
About ten minutes, most of it the test suite.

_Drafted with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23. Every command was run on the
project's machine on those days with the results described here; the figures and the pipeline run
went to a scratch folder instead of `data/figures-demo` and `data/outputs-demo`, and the fresh-clone
commands ran in a copy of the repository's committed files, without `data/`._

**Before you start.** Python 3.12, Java 17 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); run everything from
the repository root. Steps 2 to 4 use data under `data/`, which is not in Git and exists only on the
machine that produced it; from a fresh clone, see [From a fresh clone](#from-a-fresh-clone).

## 1. Tests

```bash
uv sync
uv run --group measure --group plots pytest
```

Every test passes, without network, in about five minutes.

## 2. The figures and their check

```bash
uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots --check
uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots --out data/figures-demo
diff -rq docs/figures data/figures-demo && echo identical
```

The first command prints each figure's checked numbers, then `documented values: compared for M1,
…, X4: all match`: every number it compares with spec §8, data-sources.md and the experiment
documents is the same. Its last line, `measurement CSVs: 4 of 4 copies identical to their sources
under data/`, says that the committed copies that X1–X4 read
([measurements/](measurements/README.md)) still equal the collectors' outputs. The second command
redraws the twelve figures and `figures.json`, and `diff` compares them with the committed ones: in
the same environment they are byte-identical. [results.md](results.md) shows the figures with the
findings and limitations.

## 3. The SQL analyses of the run of record

```bash
RUN=data/outputs/windows/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s21-r2/run-20261013T043848Z-2
uv run python analysis/sql_overview.py $RUN
uv run python analysis/sql_comparison.py $RUN
uv run python analysis/sql_sensitivity.py $RUN
```

About 10 s each. Their last tables hold the numbers of spec §8 and of the table in results.md,
section 2: for example 529, 466, 311, 174 and 310 windows, the 2x return above twice the 1x return
in 219 of AAPL's 517 compared windows, and TSLA's median 2x return of −12.3% (`-0.1225…`)
without the windows that use an unverified day. `sql_overview.py` also prints the `paired`
schema, a few rows and the physical plan of its query.

## 4. A small pipeline run and its independent check

```bash
uv run python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/full-2026-10-12/calendar-year-r2 --out-root data/outputs-demo --run-id demo-1
uv run python -m etf_risk.verify --run data/outputs-demo/full-2026-10-12/calendar-year-r2/demo-1
```

The first runs the model in Spark over the 151 calendar-year windows, a labeled supplement to the
rolling windows, with every check at full scale, in about 20 s: it prints `demo-1: ok` with the row
counts (151 windows, 75,971 path-day rows) and the run folder, then `ok` for each of the ten groups
of checks. The second compares a sample of windows with an independent Python computation (53
windows and 106 paths on 2026-10-23) and reports 0 mismatches; both find the one breached window,
AAPL's calendar year 2000. The outputs go to `data/outputs-demo/`, outside Git; nothing is
overwritten, so another run needs a new `--run-id`.

## From a fresh clone

The tests need no data, and neither do figures X1–X4, which read the committed measurement CSVs:

```bash
uv sync
uv run --group measure --group plots pytest
uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots --check --figures X1 X2 X3 X4
```

documented values describe, are:

|---|---|---|
